# Admin audit log

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:admin-audit-log` · **Epic:** [#37](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/37) · **Tickets:** 4 (2S 2M)

Every admin change made through the CP console or API, plus logins, is recorded with who did it, what changed, and state hashes before and after. Entries are hash-chained and signed with Ed25519, using the existing receipt signer. Admins can list and verify the log in the dashboard or offline with a CLI, and each entry is also emitted as a `warden.admin.v1` JSON log line so an off-host copy anchors the chain. The feature is CP-only and off by default.

## How we build it

- New package `internal/adminaudit` holds the `Entry` type, its canonical encoder, the SQLite `Store` on the `internal/cpstate` DB (W-P1-SSO-01), `Verify`, and `Recorder.Record(ctx, Entry)` as the single write API. The HTTP middleware, the auth handlers, the offline CLIs (W-P1-WTOK-03 token CLI) and later features (P2 token service and key manager, P4 grants, P5 KMS and retention) all write through Recorder, so none of them import `internal/controlplane`. `internal/controlplane` keeps only the middleware, the per-target state hashers and the wiring.
- Enabled only when `--state-dir` is set and the new CP-local `console.adminAudit.enabled` is true (default false in P1). When disabled, no table, key file or middleware is created and CP behaviour is byte-identical to today. Workers never run this code; worker-local dashboard writes stay out of scope.
- cpstate migration `admin_audit(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts_unix_nano INTEGER, actor_id, actor_role, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, details_json, outcome, http_status, before_hash, after_hash, client_ip, request_id, key_id, prev_hash, entry_hash, signature)` with indexes on ts, action and actor_id, plus a side table `admin_audit_actor(seq PRIMARY KEY, sub, email)`. actor_id = HMAC-SHA256(cp salt, sub), so plaintext identity sits outside the signed bytes and P5 retention can erase side rows without breaking the chain. No code path issues UPDATE or DELETE on either table. auth_method is one of oidc|breakglass|cli|none|system, validated in Go rather than with a SQLite CHECK, so later phases can add values without a table rebuild.
- Canonical bytes are `encoding/json` of a fixed-order struct: v, seq, ts_unix_nano, actor_id, actor_role, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, details, outcome, http_status, before_hash, after_hash, client_ip, request_id, key_id, prev_hash. entry_hash = sha256(canonical), so prev_hash is covered. signature = Ed25519 over the domain-separated message "warden.admin.v1\x00" || entry_hash, through new `audit.Signer.SignBytes` and `audit.VerifyBytes`; `Sign(event)` stays byte-identical. Seq 1 is an `audit.genesis` entry with prev_hash of 32 zero bytes. Order comes from seq; ts is informational, so clock steps never break verification. A golden-bytes test pins the encoding.
- The chain stays linear across processes: Append runs in one SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads the head row, builds and signs seq+1, inserts and commits. The CP and the offline token CLI can append to the same DB at the same time. A later Postgres store does the same under a row or advisory lock.
- Key handling: new exported `audit.LoadOrCreateSigner(path)` (a port of the unexported worker `loadOrCreateSigner` in internal/worker/wiring.go) creates the PKCS#8 key with O_CREATE|O_EXCL at 0600 and re-reads it if another process won the race. The key defaults to `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`, and the new `--admin-audit-key-file` flag lets it live on a separate secret mount. Every row stores key_id (hex of the first 8 bytes of sha256(pubkey)). Startup fails closed if rows exist and the key file is missing or its key_id differs from the head row, instead of silently minting a new key. P1 ships one key and no rotation command; the supported rotation (`admin-audit rotate-key` with an old-key-signed handoff entry) is W-P2-KEYS-06 in p2-key-manager. Until then a documented manual rotation starts a new chain segment: with the CP stopped, the operator runs `admin-audit verify` and `admin-audit export` (W-P1-AAUD-04) to archive the old segment and its public key, puts the new key at `--admin-audit-key-file`, and starts the CP once with `--admin-audit-new-segment=<new key_id>`. The CP then appends an `audit.segment_start` entry signed by the new key, whose prev_hash is the old head entry_hash and whose details name the previous key_id; every later row is stamped with the new key_id. The flag must equal the loaded key's key_id and is a no-op once the head is on that key, so a restart can never rotate the key by accident. The key and DB share a trust boundary until p2-key-manager or p5-kms replace the signer behind a small interface.
- Capture is route-table driven, not method driven. AAUD-02 extends the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route entries with `Action`, `Target` and `Audited bool`. The middleware wraps only /dashboard/*, /central/secrets* and /auth/logout, never /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /healthz. Audited today: policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders, /dashboard/api/secretstore POST/DELETE and /central/secrets POST/DELETE. Worker tokens, the block list and policy versions register their own routes and hashers when they land. Read-only POSTs (/dashboard/api/query, /dashboard/api/query/generate, /dashboard/api/audit/verify, admin-audit/verify) are `Audited:false`. A test fails if any registered route has no classification.
- Middleware order: session (sets Principal), then request id, then admin audit, then authz, then handler. Audited requests take one CP-wide admin-mutation mutex (30s context timeout) around before-hash, handler, after-hash and append, so the hashes describe exactly this change; admin writes are rare and the lock never touches worker routes. The middleware never reads request bodies. Handlers attach a non-secret `target_ref` and closed-allowlist `details` through `adminaudit.Annotate(ctx, ref, details)`, for example `secret:OPENAI_KEY` or `policy@<etag>`.
- State hashers are HMAC-SHA256 with a CP-local key, so low-entropy config cannot be guessed offline from a hash. Built-in hashers cover the policy, settings, integrations, detection and llmproviders blocks. Secret stores keep state outside Warden, so their hashes are empty and only the operation and key name are recorded. Secret values, any substring of them, and `secrets.Ref` output never enter a row, log line or detail.
- Outcomes: ok (2xx/3xx), denied (401/403/CSRF failure on an authenticated session), rejected (other 4xx, including 409), error (5xx). On error the after hash is still taken, because a change may have partly applied. Requests with no session are never chained, so nobody can flood the table; they get a rate-limited log line only.
- Non-HTTP events go through Recorder. Hand edits of the served YAML are audited in both policy-store modes: in file mode (the default) the existing 3s re-read compares the served file hash with the hash the last CP writer produced, and a change no CP writer made appends one `config.external_change` row (auth_method system, target policy, before `file:<old sha256>`, after `file:<new sha256>`) once per distinct hash; versioned mode records the same action through W-P1-PVER-05. Also through Recorder: the auth handlers record `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed` and `auth.logout`; W-P1-OPS1-01 records every `auth.breakglass` attempt; offline CLIs record auth_method `cli` with actor `cli:<os user>`. In `console.auth: none` mode the actor is `anonymous` with auth_method `none`. client_ip is RemoteAddr unless the peer is in the new CP-local `console.trustedProxies` CIDR list (default empty), which allows X-Forwarded-For. request_id is a valid incoming X-Request-Id (64 chars or fewer of [A-Za-z0-9-]) or a newly generated id, echoed in the response.
- Failure mode is fail-closed for audited mutations only. If the store health flag is bad, the middleware returns 503 `admin_audit_unavailable` before the handler runs. If an append fails after a successful change, the entry is logged at ERROR with `persist_failed=true`, the store is marked degraded until an append succeeds, and an `admin_audit_degraded` Finding is published through the CP alert pipeline. Reads, /policy serving, ingest and heartbeats never depend on audit health.
- SIEM and anchoring: each entry is emitted through an `adminaudit.Emitter` seam whose default writes slog JSON `msg=admin_audit schema=warden.admin.v1` with seq, entry_hash, prev_hash and key_id plus plaintext sub and email. A periodic `admin_audit.checkpoint` line (head seq and entry_hash, default every 5m) lets an off-host copy detect tail truncation or a rollback from backup. W-P1-JAUD-03 plugs the `auditlog.Writer` into the Emitter seam; this feature only logs to the CP logger.
- Verification: one `adminaudit.Verify(fromSeq, toSeq, anchor)` checks seq continuity, prev_hash links, entry_hash, the signature for each key_id (a key_id change is accepted only at an `audit.segment_start` entry, or at the `audit.key_rotated` entry W-P2-KEYS-06 adds), and the actor HMAC where a side row exists. It streams rows, caps work per call and returns `lastVerifiedSeq` so large ranges resume. The dashboard handler and the offline `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` CLI share it. At startup the CP verifies the last 1000 rows and the head signature and publishes `admin_audit_verify_failed` on failure. A signed `audit.pruned` checkpoint entry type is reserved so P5 retention can drop a prefix without breaking verification. The table grows without bound in P1; it holds admin actions only.

## Done when

On a CP started with --state-dir, console.auth=oidc and console.adminAudit.enabled=true, editing policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders and secrets (both /dashboard/api/secretstore and /central/secrets) each produces exactly one chained, signed row with actor, role, auth_method, target_ref and before/after hashes. OIDC logins and an authenticated viewer's denied write also produce rows, while heartbeats, ingest and read-only POSTs produce none. No secret value or secrets.Ref string appears in any row or log line. An admin can list, filter and verify the log in the dashboard (a viewer gets 403) and with `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` while the CP is stopped. Changing any column or deleting a middle row fails verification, a swapped key file stops the CP from starting (the documented manual rotation leaves a verifiable `audit.segment_start` boundary instead), and deleting the newest rows is caught against the seq/entry_hash anchor in the emitted log lines. With the audit DB unwritable, mutations return 503 and a Finding fires while /policy keeps serving. A hand edit of the served YAML in file mode writes one config.external_change row with the new file hash.

### 1/4 · W-P1-AAUD-01

**Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#38](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/38)

Add the new `internal/adminaudit` package with the canonical `Entry`, the SQLite store on cpstate, `Verify`, and `Recorder` as the only write API. Appends run in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction so the CP and offline CLIs can share the chain without forking it. Add domain-separated `SignBytes`/`VerifyBytes` to the existing receipt signer and an exported, race-safe key loader. Nothing records entries yet, so behaviour does not change.

**Requirements**

- Add `(*audit.Signer).SignBytes(b []byte) []byte` and `audit.VerifyBytes(pub ed25519.PublicKey, b, sig []byte) bool` in internal/audit/receipt.go; both use the message "warden.admin.v1\x00" || b. `Sign(event)` output and the receipt format do not change.
- Add exported `audit.LoadOrCreateSigner(path string) (*Signer, error)` that creates the PKCS#8 key with O_CREATE|O_EXCL at 0600, re-reads the file if it already exists, and rejects non-Ed25519 keys. internal/worker is not changed.
- Register cpstate migrations for `admin_audit` and `admin_audit_actor` with the columns and indexes in the design. No Go code issues UPDATE or DELETE on either table.
- Canonical bytes are JSON of a fixed-order `Entry` struct with `v:1` and ts as an INTEGER unix-nano; entry_hash = sha256(canonical) with prev_hash inside canonical; seq 1 is `audit.genesis` with a 32-zero-byte prev_hash; key_id is hex of the first 8 bytes of sha256(pubkey); actor_id = HMAC-SHA256(cp salt, sub).
- `Store.Append` reads the head, signs and inserts seq+1 inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. `List(filter, limit<=200, cursor)` is newest-first with a seq cursor. `Verify(fromSeq, toSeq, anchor)` streams rows and returns {ok, checked, firstBadSeq, headSeq, headHash, lastVerifiedSeq}.
- Startup check `Store.Open` fails with an actionable error when rows exist and the key is missing or its key_id differs from the head row. Add the `--admin-audit-key-file` flag (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`). The only exception is the manual rotation: with `--admin-audit-new-segment=<key_id>` equal to the loaded key's key_id and a head row on another key_id, Open appends one `audit.segment_start` entry (signed by the new key, prev_hash = head entry_hash, details {previous_key_id}) and continues. A value that does not match the loaded key fails startup, and the flag is a no-op once the head is on that key. Scheduled or automatic rotation is out of scope for P1 (W-P2-KEYS-06).
- The store is built in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go only when `--state-dir` is set and `console.adminAudit.enabled` is true (default false), and is passed as a new `controlplane.Config.AdminAudit`. The CP logs the public key and key_id at INFO; the private key and PEM are never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/audit/receipt.go: add `SignBytes` and `VerifyBytes` (new) with the domain-separation prefix; leave `Sign`, `Verify` and `Receipt` unchanged.
2. New internal/audit/keyfile.go: `LoadOrCreateSigner(path)` ported from internal/worker/wiring.go `loadOrCreateSigner`, using O_CREATE|O_EXCL and a re-read on EEXIST.
3. New internal/adminaudit/entry.go: `Entry` struct in canonical field order, `canonical()`, `entryHash()`, actor HMAC helper, outcome and auth_method validation.
4. New internal/adminaudit/store.go: cpstate migrations, `Store` with `Append` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), `List`, `Head`, and the startup key_id check; new `Recorder` interface wrapping Append.
5. New internal/adminaudit/verify.go: streaming `Verify` with anchor support and per-call row cap.
6. internal/config: add `console.adminAudit.enabled`. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add `--admin-audit-key-file`, build the store when enabled, set `controlplane.Config.AdminAudit` (new field, nil means disabled).
7. Tests: internal/adminaudit/store_test.go (concurrency, two `*sql.DB` handles, tamper table, middle and tail deletion with anchor, key mismatch), entry_test.go (golden bytes), internal/audit/keyfile_test.go and receipt_test.go additions.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] 1000 Appends from 50 goroutines plus a second Store opened on the same DB file produce a chain where Verify returns ok=true, checked=1001 (with genesis) and no seq gaps: `go test -race ./internal/adminaudit -run TestStoreConcurrentAppend`
- [ ] Changing any single column of row N in SQL, or deleting row N from the middle, makes Verify return ok=false with firstBadSeq=N; deleting the last row passes a plain Verify but fails Verify with the previous head as anchor: `go test ./internal/adminaudit -run 'TestStoreTamper|TestStoreAnchor'`
- [ ] A golden test pins the canonical bytes and entry_hash of a fixed Entry, and a signature from `Sign(event)` over the same bytes fails `VerifyBytes`: `go test ./internal/adminaudit ./internal/audit -run 'TestCanonicalGolden|TestSignBytes|TestVerifyBytes'`
- [ ] `LoadOrCreateSigner` creates a 0600 file, returns the same key on reload, rejects a non-Ed25519 key, and two concurrent calls on a new path return the same public key.
- [ ] Opening a store that has rows with a different key file returns an error naming the expected key_id, and the existing receipt tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] With `console.adminAudit.enabled` false or no --state-dir, no admin_audit table or key file is created, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] A store whose head is on key A, opened with key B and `--admin-audit-new-segment=<B key_id>`, appends exactly one audit.segment_start row and Verify returns ok across both segments; the next start with the same flag writes nothing, and a flag value that is not B's key_id fails startup: `go test ./internal/adminaudit -run TestNewSegmentRotation`

### 2/4 · W-P1-AAUD-02

**Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#39](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/39)

Add the admin audit middleware to the CP, driven by `Action`, `Target` and `Audited` fields added to the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table rather than by HTTP method, so worker heartbeats, ingest and read-only POSTs are never chained. It serializes admin mutations, records before/after HMAC state hashes and the outcome, and fails closed when the store cannot write. Auth handlers record logins and logouts through the same Recorder, and every entry is emitted as a `warden.admin.v1` slog line through a seam that W-P1-JAUD-03 later points at the JSON audit writer.

**Requirements**

- Extend the SSO-05 `authzRoute` entries with `Action`, `Target` and `Audited bool`. Audited routes: dashboard policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders, /dashboard/api/secretstore POST/DELETE, /central/secrets POST and /central/secrets/{key} DELETE. Read-only POSTs are `Audited:false`. /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest and /healthz are never wrapped.
- Order is session, request id, admin audit, authz, handler. A 403 or CSRF failure for an authenticated principal is recorded as outcome=denied; a request with no session writes no row and only a rate-limited log line.
- Take one CP-wide admin-mutation mutex (30s context timeout) across before-hash, handler, after-hash and append. Expose `RegisterStateHasher(target, fn)`; built-in HMAC hashers cover policy, settings, integrations, detection and llmproviders; secrets record empty hashes plus the key name. Worker-token and blocked-user hashers are registered by W-P1-WTOK-03 and W-P1-BLOCK-03.
- The middleware never reads r.Body. Handlers set `target_ref` and allowlisted `details` through `adminaudit.Annotate`. No secret value, substring of one, `secrets.Ref` string, bearer token or body appears in a row, log line or detail.
- Fail closed: if the store health flag is bad, return 503 `{"error":"admin_audit_unavailable"}` before the handler runs. If Append fails after the handler, log the entry at ERROR with `persist_failed=true`, mark the store degraded until an append succeeds, and publish an `admin_audit_degraded` Finding.
- request_id is a valid incoming X-Request-Id or a new id, echoed in the response. client_ip is RemoteAddr unless the peer is in `console.trustedProxies` (default empty). With `console.auth: none` the actor is `anonymous` and auth_method `none`.
- Auth handlers record `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed` and `auth.logout`. Every entry goes through `adminaudit.Emitter`; the default writes slog JSON `msg=admin_audit schema=warden.admin.v1` with seq, entry_hash, prev_hash and key_id, and a checkpoint line with head seq and hash every 5m.
- File-mode external edits: atomicWriteConfig records the sha256 of the bytes each CP writer wrote. When the 3s re-read in file mode loads a served config.yaml whose hash differs from both the last loaded hash and the last CP-written hash, one `config.external_change` row is appended through the Recorder (auth_method system, actor `system`, target policy, before `file:<previous sha256>`, after `file:<new sha256>`), once per distinct hash, and the new policy is served as today. No file content is logged or stored.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/authz.go (from SSO-05): add `Action`, `Target`, `Audited` to the route struct and fill them in; extend the route-coverage test so every route has a classification and every audited route has Action and Target.
2. New internal/adminaudit/annotate.go and emitter.go: `Annotate(ctx, ref, details)`, the context carrier, the `Emitter` interface and the slog implementation, plus the checkpoint ticker.
3. New internal/controlplane/adminaudit_mw.go: request-id middleware, `adminAuditMiddleware`, the admin-mutation mutex, the status-capturing ResponseWriter, outcome mapping, the trustedProxies client_ip helper and the health flag; add `console.trustedProxies` (CIDR list, default empty) to ConsoleConfig in internal/config/console.go.
4. New internal/controlplane/adminaudit_hash.go: `RegisterStateHasher` and HMAC hashers for policy, settings, integrations, detection (`currentDetectionConfig()`) and llmproviders blocks.
5. Annotate target_ref in `handleSecrets`/`handleSecretByKey` (internal/controlplane/secrets.go), dashboard `handleSecretStore` (internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go) and the policy save handler (policy@<etag>).
6. `Server.Handler()` in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: wrap /dashboard/, /central/secrets* and /auth/logout in the chain only when `cfg.AdminAudit != nil`. Add Recorder calls to the SSO-04 login, callback-failure and logout handlers.
7. Tests in internal/controlplane/adminaudit_mw_test.go covering every audited route, skipped routes, denied and unauthenticated requests, the secret-leak canary, concurrency and the 503 path.
8. internal/controlplane: record the written hash in atomicWriteConfig and compare it in the file-mode re-read loop in Server.Start, calling Recorder.Record for an external change.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Every authz entry with `Audited:true`, called by an admin, writes exactly one row with the expected action, target and outcome=ok: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminAuditAllAuditedRoutes`
- [ ] 100 POST /control/heartbeat, 100 POST /central/ingest and 10 each of POST /dashboard/api/query, /query/generate and /audit/verify leave the row count unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminAuditSkipsWorkerAndReadOnlyRoutes`
- [ ] A viewer POST to /dashboard/api/policy returns 403 and writes one row with outcome=denied, http_status=403 and before_hash equal to after_hash; the same POST with no session returns 401 and writes no row.

### 3/4 · W-P1-AAUD-03

**Show admin audit log and chain verification in the dashboard**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#40](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/40)

Add admin-only API routes and an 'Admin log' tab so admins can browse, filter and verify the chain and copy the public key. The dashboard cannot import controlplane, so wiring goes through a `dashboard.AdminAuditSource` interface set only on the CP; workers and disabled CPs return 404. The tab stays separate from the existing receipts 'Audit' tab and its `/dashboard/api/audit*` routes.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/admin-audit?actor=&action=&outcome=&since=&cursor=&limit=` (admin) returns {entries, nextCursor} newest-first; limit defaults to 50, maximum 200; since is RFC3339; a malformed parameter returns 400.
- `POST /dashboard/api/admin-audit/verify` (admin, `Audited:false`) returns {ok, checked, firstBadSeq, headSeq, headHash, lastVerifiedSeq}, accepts an optional {fromSeq, anchor}, caps rows per call, and allows one run at a time (a concurrent call gets 429).
- `GET /dashboard/api/admin-audit/pubkey` (any authenticated role) returns {alg:"ed25519", keys:[{keyId, publicKey}]} for every key_id seen in the table.
- Wiring uses `(*dashboard.Server).SetAdminAudit(src AdminAuditSource)`, an interface defined in internal/dashboard; with no source all three routes return 404 and the tab is hidden.
- The 'Admin log' tab in internal/dashboard/index.html has actor, action and outcome filters, paging, a Verify button and the public key with copy; every rendered field goes through `esc()`.
- Responses never include request bodies or signature bytes, and errors return generic messages.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/dashboard/dashboard_adminaudit.go: `AdminAuditSource` interface (List, Verify, PubKeys), view structs, `SetAdminAudit`, and the three handlers with a verify semaphore.
2. Register the routes in `dashboard.Server.Handler()` (internal/dashboard/dashboard.go) next to, but distinct from, `/dashboard/api/audit`.
3. Add the three routes to the SSO-05 authz table at the right roles, with verify marked `Audited:false`, so the route-coverage test passes.
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go `Handler()`: call `dash.SetAdminAudit` with an adapter over `cfg.AdminAudit` when it is not nil.
5. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the 'Admin log' tab, shown when `/auth/me` role is admin and the API does not return 404.
6. Tests in internal/dashboard/dashboard_adminaudit_test.go with a fake source; update docs/control-plane.md with the routes and the verify flow.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With 120 rows, three GETs with limit=50 following nextCursor return 50, 50 and 20 entries in strictly descending seq order with no duplicates, and a viewer or editor gets 403: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestAdminAuditAPI`
- [ ] Verify on an untouched store returns {ok:true, checked: row count}; with row 7 tampered it returns {ok:false, firstBadSeq:7}.
- [ ] A dashboard.Server with no SetAdminAudit call returns 404 on all three routes: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestAdminAuditNotWired`
- [ ] Two simultaneous verify requests return one 200 and one 429.
- [ ] The pubkey response matches the CP signer's `PubKey()` and the key_id stored in rows, and an actor email of `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` renders as literal text in the tab.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#14--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#58--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route

### 4/4 · W-P1-AAUD-04

**Add offline admin audit verify and export CLI**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#232](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/232)

Add `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` and `admin-audit export` subcommands that open the cpstate DB read-only, so an operator can check the chain after a restore (p1-breakglass) or during an incident with the CP down, and an auditor can verify an export without CP access. Both use the same `adminaudit.Verify` as the dashboard. Also run a bounded verification at CP startup so tampering is flagged early.

**Requirements**

- `warden control-plane admin-audit verify --state-dir <dir> [--from-seq N] [--anchor seq:hash]` opens `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` read-only, prints {ok, checked, firstBadSeq, headSeq, headHash} and exits non-zero on failure.
- `warden control-plane admin-audit export --state-dir <dir> --out <file>` writes JSONL of chained entries plus a `keys` record with every public key and key_id; it never writes the side-table sub or email unless `--include-identity` is set.
- `adminaudit.VerifyExport(path)` verifies an export file with no DB, using the same checks as `Verify`.
- At CP startup with the store enabled, verify the last 1000 rows and the head signature; on failure log at ERROR and publish an `admin_audit_verify_failed` Finding without blocking /policy serving.
- The CLI never opens the DB for writing and never reads or prints the private key.
- New docs/runbooks/admin-audit-key.md documents the P1 manual rotation: stop the CP, `admin-audit verify`, `admin-audit export` (keep the export and old public key off-host), install the new key, start once with `--admin-audit-new-segment=<new key_id>`, then verify again. It states that P1 ships one key with no rotation command and that W-P2-KEYS-06 replaces this procedure with `admin-audit rotate-key`.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/adminaudit/export.go: JSONL encoder, `keys` record, and `VerifyExport`.
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the `admin-audit` subcommand with `verify` and `export`, opening the DB with cpstate.OpenReadOnly from W-P1-SSO-01.
3. internal/controlplane: run the bounded startup verify after the store opens and publish the Finding through the existing alert pipeline.
4. Tests in internal/adminaudit/export_test.go and a CLI test in cmd/proxy; document both commands in docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] On a seeded state dir, `go run ./cmd/proxy control-plane admin-audit verify --state-dir <dir>` exits 0 and prints ok=true; after one row is altered it exits 1 and prints its seq.
- [ ] An export of 500 rows verifies with `VerifyExport`, and altering one line makes it fail at that seq: `go test ./internal/adminaudit -run TestExportRoundTrip`
- [ ] Verify with `--anchor` set to a previous head detects deletion of the newest rows.
- [ ] The export file contains no sub or email values unless `--include-identity` is passed, and the DB file's mtime is unchanged after verify and export.
- [ ] A CP started on a DB with a tampered row in the last 1000 publishes `admin_audit_verify_failed` and still serves GET /policy with 200.
- [ ] An export spanning an `audit.segment_start` entry lists both public keys in its `keys` record and passes `VerifyExport`, and the same export with the segment_start line removed fails at that seq.
